landing.faq_title: Frequently asked questions about QR digital menus
landing.faq_subtitle: Everything restaurant and café owners ask before placing QR codes on tables.
landing.faq1_q: What is a QR Code digital menu and how does it work?
landing.faq1_a: It is a fast mobile web page that opens when guests point their phone camera at a printed table QR code. You manage dishes, photos, and prices in your dashboard behind one permanent link.
landing.faq2_q: Do customers need to download an app to view the menu?
landing.faq2_a: No. Your menu opens directly inside the standard Safari or Chrome browser on any Android or iPhone in seconds—no app download or guest sign-up required.
landing.faq3_q: If I change prices or dishes, do I have to reprint the QR code?
landing.faq3_a: No. Your /c/your-business address stays permanent once published. You update prices, photos, and sold-out badges anytime while keeping the exact same printed table cards.
landing.faq4_q: Can I import my current PDF or printed menu photo?
landing.faq4_a: Yes. Our built-in OCR importer extracts categories, item names, and prices from digital PDFs, menu photos, or pasted text straight into a draft.
landing.faq5_q: Does the menu support Portuguese, English, and Spanish?
landing.faq5_a: Yes. Both the interface and optional category and dish translations switch between Portuguese, English, and Spanish with zero page reload.
landing.faq6_q: How does QR Cardápio help get more Google Maps reviews?
landing.faq6_a: Paste your Google Maps profile or direct Google review link in Settings to show a native review invitation card at the bottom of your published menu.
landing.faq7_q: How much does QR Cardápio cost and are there per-order fees?
landing.faq7_a: There are zero per-scan or per-order commissions. You can build and preview drafts freely, and when monthly billing is enabled, the Essential Plan is a flat R$ 29.90 per month.
landing.faq8_q: What is the minimum recommended print size for table QR codes?
landing.faq8_a: Print the QR square at 3×3 cm (1.2×1.2 in) or larger, keep the white outer border uncropped, and prefer matte lamination to prevent ceiling glare.
